definition_notes: Penn's CDS B1 reports only what Penn calls its 'adjusted total enrollment': degree-seeking students in traditional programs (UG in SAS/ENG/NUR/WH; graduate degree programs). Per Penn's Quick Facts documentation (Fall 2023 edition) it excludes non-traditional students in the School of Liberal & Professional Studies, the Wharton Evening Program, the Accelerated Nursing Program and stand-alone certificate programs; the Fall 2024 edition says it excludes online, non-traditional and non-credential-seeking students. Penn's own all-credit-bearing 'Enrollment Total' in Quick Facts is 28,201 (Fall 2022), 28,711 (Fall 2023) and 29,109 (Fall 2024), which equal IPEDS. The CDS counts equal Penn's own adjusted totals (Fall 2024: UG 10,013 + graduate 14,010 = 24,023; Fall 2023: 9,995 + 13,795 = 23,790).
caveats: Gap vs IPEDS is -17.1% in Fall 2023 (23,790 vs 28,711) and -17.5% vs Penn Quick Facts Fall 2024 (24,023 vs 29,109). Explained by Penn's own documentation: IPEDS/Quick Facts 'Enrollment Total' counts all credit-bearing students (Fall 2024: 1,465 'Other Undergraduate' and 3,621 other graduate students beyond the adjusted total); the CDS counts only traditional degree-seeking students. Quick Facts PDFs saved in the Penn folder.

Original-slide FY23 count 23,374 equals the CDS Fall 2022 figure exactly, so the slide series was already on this narrower CDS/adjusted basis. If Brett wants all-enrolled students (IPEDS basis) the Penn numbers are 28,201 / 28,711 / 29,109.
Penn Quick Facts Fall 2024 documentation table header reads 'Enrollment Total (Fall 2023)' but the values (10,013 and 14,010) are Fall 2024; a typo in the source, values match the CDS 2024-25.
